chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him: 'What is the ascetism (zuhd) in the world?' He said: 'Woe to you! It is its forbidden things (haram), so avoid them.'

key_terms.الزُّهْدُ: zuhd — the Islamic concept of ascetism or detachment from worldly things, understood here not as poverty but as avoidance of the forbidden
key_terms.حَرَامَهَا: haramuha — the forbidden things of the world; haram refers to what is explicitly prohibited by Islamic law
key_terms.فَتَنَكَّبْهُ: fatanakkabhu — avoid it, steer clear of it; the verb tanakkaba implies deliberate avoidance and turning away
key_terms.وَيْحَكَ: waylaka/wayhaka — an Arabic exclamation of astonishment or mild rebuke, implying the questioner's misconception needs correction

ai.seo_question: What is the true meaning of zuhd (ascetism) in Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) redefines zuhd (ascetism) in a remarkably concise and practical way: true ascetism is not about renouncing all worldly pleasures or adopting a life of extreme austerity, but simply about avoiding what Allah has prohibited. This teaching, narrated through al-Sakuni — a Sunni transmitter whose Shia-related narrations were generally accepted — reflects the Imam's characteristic approach of presenting Islamic obligations in their simplest and most actionable form. The original audience, who may have associated zuhd with monastic withdrawal, would have found this definition both liberating and demanding: liberating because it permits worldly enjoyment, and demanding because it requires constant vigilance over haram.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is the ascetism in the world?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Woe be unto you! It’s the Prohibitions, so keep away from it (the Prohibitions)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from af-Nawfafiy from af-Sakuniy who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the meaning of restraint from worldly matters.
He (the Imam) said, Tie upon you! It is (not difficult to understand) knowing what is unlawful so that you can avoid it.’”
